name: NL2Repo-Bench
intro: NL2Repo-Bench是一个旨在评估编码智能体长周期代码仓库生成能力的基准测试。它要求智能体根据自然语言需求文档，自主设计架构、管理依赖、实现多模块逻辑并生成可安装的Python库。实验表明，现有模型在长周期仓库生成方面表现不佳，平均测试通过率低于40%。该基准测试揭示了长周期推理是下一代自主编码智能体的关键瓶颈。
org: Tsinghua University, Beijing Institute of Technology, Peking University, Renmin University of China,
build_method: GitHub 仓库筛选, AST 辅助需求逆向, 专家与静态覆盖审核, Agent 先导验证
metric: Average Test Pass Rate, Fully Passed Pass@1 Count
eval_feature: 空工作区从零构建, 隐藏源码与测试, 上游 pytest 执行评测
build_method_en: GitHub Repository Selection, AST-Assisted Specification Reverse Engineering, Expert and Static-Coverage Review, Pilot-Agent Validation
eval_feature_en: From-Scratch Empty-Workspace Generation, Hidden Source and Tests, Upstream-pytest Execution
intro_en: NL2Repo-Bench is a benchmark designed to evaluate the long-term code repository generation capabilities of coding agents. It requires agents to autonomously design architecture, manage dependencies, implement multi-module logic, and generate installable Python libraries based on natural language requirement documents. Experiments show that existing models perform poorly in long-term repository generation, with an average test pass rate below 40%. This benchmark reveals that long-term reasoning is a key bottleneck for the next generation of autonomous coding agents.
metric_en: Average Test Pass Rate, Fully Passed Pass@1 Count
drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2512.12730v2. Candidate Python libraries must have 300-120,000 LOC, at least 10 stars, native pytest tests, and recent creation or updates; annotators retain only repositories whose upstream tests pass. An AST scanner inventories classes, functions, and signatures, which annotators reverse-engineer into a four-part requirements document. Expert review, static API coverage, verified Docker environments, pilot coding agents, and senior-engineer failure analysis drive refinement until valid. The release contains 104 tasks across nine categories. Agents receive only one document in an empty workspace, with no scaffold, source, tests, or signatures, then generated installable libraries are scored by the original upstream pytest suite using average test pass rate and fully passed Pass@1 count.
